scientific_question: How do intrinsic basicity, resonance, sterics, site multiplicity, and HF cluster size control HF association and proton transfer in isolated amine-HF clusters?

entries.name: ammonia
entries.hypothesis: Weakest nitrogen-base anchor; additional HF should most clearly expose cluster cooperativity.

entries.name: methylamine
entries.hypothesis: One methyl group should strengthen proton acceptance relative to ammonia while retaining low steric shielding.

entries.name: dimethylamine
entries.hypothesis: Higher intrinsic basicity than methylamine should compete with increasing methyl crowding.

entries.name: trimethylamine
entries.hypothesis: High gas-phase basicity should favor the ion-pair endpoint, while three methyl groups may alter the approach geometry.

entries.name: triethylamine
entries.hypothesis: A strong but more shielded site tests whether HF capture and barrier height depart from proton-affinity ordering.

entries.name: aniline
entries.hypothesis: Resonance lowers intrinsic basicity and should weaken proton transfer despite an accessible nitrogen.

entries.name: pyridine
entries.hypothesis: An accessible aromatic lone pair provides a contrast to resonance-delocalized aniline at similar molecular size.

entries.name: imidazole
entries.hypothesis: The pyridine-like nitrogen should be active while the pyrrolic nitrogen must remain excluded.

entries.name: 1,4-diazabicyclo[2.2.2]octane
entries.hypothesis: Two symmetry-related nitrogens test site deduplication and possible second-site stabilization by larger HF clusters.

entries.name: dimethyl_ether
entries.hypothesis: A weaker oxygen base should remain dominated by molecular HF association and calibrate false activation claims.
